The database adapter contract - feature 3 of the feature audit.
VERDICT: REDESIGN. This replaces a 20-method list assembled from PHP's and
Node's existing interfaces. That list was wrong in a way none of the four
frameworks could show on its own, and only implementing it surfaced why:
- DDL was never an adapter concern. PHP builds CREATE TABLE in ORM.php,
Node in migration.ts, Python in model.py. createTable/addColumn were
about to be added to fifteen adapters for a job all four already do
ABOVE the adapter.
- CRUD is not engine-specific, and duplicating it costs 4.3x. Measured:
Ruby 1335 LOC / 142 functions against PHP 5823 / 438, same job, seven
drivers against ten adapters.
- Dialect translation already lives outside the adapter in all four.
AN ADAPTER IS ONLY WHAT GENUINELY DIFFERS PER ENGINE. Everything else - SQL
building, DDL, pagination, filters, translation - lives above it, once.
EVERY METHOD IS REQUIRED. There are no optional members. An optional method
forces the caller to feature-detect, which is Node's `?` and Ruby's
respond_to? - and both turn a missing method into a SILENT SKIP, which is
worse than a crash.

connection.why: Driver handshake, and an engine must be able to name itself. Nothing could, so callers type-checked the concrete adapter class (ORM::detectDialect) - a caller depending on the implementation rather than the contract.

methods.name: getDatabaseType
methods.note: -> canonical engine name; what the translator dispatches on

execution.why: Placeholder style, cursor handling and result shape differ per driver. Everything else that runs SQL is composed from these two.

methods.name: execute
methods.note: run a statement; RAISES on error, never returns false

transaction.why: Genuinely per-driver, including whether a standalone write commits on its own.

methods.name: autocommit
methods.note: on for a standalone write, suppressed inside an explicit transaction

introspection.why: System catalogs differ entirely between engines - PRAGMA, information_schema, RDB$RELATION_FIELDS.

diagnostics.why: Retrieving the last id and the last error is driver-specific and cannot be composed.

not_on_the_adapter._note: Each of these is composable ABOVE the adapter from execute + fetch + getDatabaseType, and each is currently duplicated per adapter in three of the four frameworks. Removing them is the bulk of the 4.3x.
not_on_the_adapter.insert: SQL building. Ruby already does it once in the facade; the other three do it in every adapter.
not_on_the_adapter.update: SQL building, plus the no-filter-is-an-error rule from feature 4 which the facade owns.
not_on_the_adapter.executeMany: a loop over execute inside one transaction.
not_on_the_adapter.fetchOne: fetch with a limit of one.
not_on_the_adapter.createTable: DDL. Already built above the adapter in all four (ORM.php, migration.ts, model.py).
not_on_the_adapter.query: a second read path nothing needs beside fetch.
not_on_the_adapter.sql_translation: the SQLTranslator unit all four already have. An adapter declares its dialect; the translator rewrites.

naming._note: Same concept, same name, idiomatic casing.
naming.python: snake_case: open, close, get_database_type, execute, fetch, start_transaction, commit, rollback, autocommit, get_tables, get_columns, table_exists, last_insert_id, error
naming.php: camelCase: open, close, getDatabaseType, execute, fetch, startTransaction, commit, rollback, autocommit, getTables, getColumns, tableExists, lastInsertId, error
